mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines a recessive trait in Mendelian inheritance?

options.A: A trait that is expressed in the phenotype only when an individual possesses two copies of the same allele (homozygous recessive).
options.B: A trait that is expressed even when only one copy of the allele is present.
options.C: A trait that can be expressed in both homozygous and heterozygous conditions.
options.D: A trait that determines the organism's sex.

mcqs.answer: A trait that is expressed in the phenotype only when an individual possesses two copies of the same allele (homozygous recessive).
mcqs.explanation: A recessive trait requires both alleles to be the same (homozygous recessive) for the trait to appear. Option B describes a dominant trait, C is incorrect because recessive traits are not expressed in heterozygotes, and D is unrelated to recessiveness.

mcqs.question: In a monohybrid cross between a true‑breeding tall pea plant (TT) and a true‑breeding dwarf plant (tt), what phenotypic ratio is expected in the F1 generation?
mcqs.explanation: All F1 offspring receive one dominant allele (T) from the tall parent and one recessive allele (t) from the dwarf parent, giving genotype Tt. Since T is dominant, every F1 plant is tall, giving a 100 % tall phenotype.

mcqs.question: Two heterozygous pea plants (Tt) are crossed. Which set of genotypes can appear among their offspring?

options.D: TT, Tt and tt can all appear

mcqs.answer: TT, Tt and tt can all appear
mcqs.explanation: A Tt × Tt cross yields a 1:2:1 genotypic ratio: 1 TT, 2 Tt, and 1 tt. Therefore all three genotypes are possible. Options A‑C are too restrictive.

mcqs.question: In a cross between heterozygous (Yy) pea plants for yellow seed colour (Y dominant), the F2 generation shows 75 yellow seeds and 25 green seeds. What are the expected phenotypic and genotypic ratios?
mcqs.explanation: A Yy × Yy cross gives a 3:1 phenotypic ratio (yellow:green) and a 1:2:1 genotypic ratio (YY:Yy:yy). The observed 75:25 numbers match this expectation. The other options do not correspond to a monohybrid cross of a dominant‑recessive pair.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about Mendel's experimental approach is a common misconception?

options.A: Mendel used pea plants because they have distinct, easily observable traits.
options.B: Mendel performed controlled crosses and kept detailed records of each generation.
options.C: Mendel knew about DNA as the hereditary material.
options.D: Mendel chose traits that assorted independently.

mcqs.answer: Mendel knew about DNA as the hereditary material.
mcqs.explanation: Mendel worked in the 19th century, long before the discovery of DNA. He inferred the existence of discrete hereditary units (genes) from his observations, but he did not know about DNA. Options A, B, and D correctly describe his methodology.

mcqs.question: Why is a trait called dominant in Mendelian genetics?

options.A: Because it is expressed in the phenotype even when only one copy of the allele is present.
options.B: Because it always appears in the genotype.
options.C: Because it masks recessive traits only in homozygous condition.
options.D: Because it is inherited exclusively from the mother.

mcqs.answer: Because it is expressed in the phenotype even when only one copy of the allele is present.
mcqs.explanation: A dominant allele produces its effect in both homozygous (AA) and heterozygous (Aa) conditions, so a single copy is sufficient for the trait to appear. Options B, C, and D are inaccurate descriptions of dominance.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares dominant and recessive traits?

options.A: A dominant trait requires two identical alleles to be expressed, whereas a recessive trait needs only one.
options.B: A dominant allele masks the effect of a recessive allele in a heterozygote, while a recessive allele is expressed only in a homozygous recessive genotype.
options.C: Recessive traits are always more common in populations than dominant traits.
options.D: Dominant traits are always expressed in the phenotype, regardless of the genotype.

mcqs.answer: A dominant allele masks the effect of a recessive allele in a heterozygote, while a recessive allele is expressed only in a homozygous recessive genotype.
mcqs.explanation: In a heterozygote (Aa), the dominant allele (A) determines the phenotype, hiding the recessive allele (a). The recessive phenotype appears only when both alleles are recessive (aa). Option A reverses the requirement, C is not a rule, and D ignores the heterozygous case.

mcqs.question: In a test cross, a plant with genotype Tt (tall) is crossed with a homozygous recessive plant (tt). If 200 offspring are obtained, how many are expected to be tall?
mcqs.explanation: A test cross of Tt × tt yields a 1:1 phenotypic ratio: 50 % tall (Tt) and 50 % dwarf (tt). With 200 offspring, 0.5 × 200 = 100 are expected to be tall. The other numbers do not match the 1:1 expectation.
